txt: Andre breaks into frenzied dance-like motion to celebrate the name. Someone turns up the beat.
Andre is busy cutting some slightly less lame, but still quite ungainly shapes on the church floor, sweating profusely.
Andre shrugs.
He doesn't even look at you.
He furrows his brow. "Fuck, man, it's difficult to get along with some people, but we're trying to make an effort. We are on a *mission* here."
He glares at you. "Yes. *Thank you*, officer."
He looks around the tent. "Aww man, but the drug lab was like an *integral* part of getting the club going."
He looks at his friend: "Shut it."
He looks at the molten toothbrush. "Maybe it was a bad idea... anyway."
He looks beat. "Okay," he nods. "What happens at the station?"
He looks to his friend, then at you. "Sorry," he nods. "I'm with Noid on this. Take us in or do it for 50%."
He nods attentively, ready to answer the questions of 'one smart cop.'
He nods enthusiastically. No doubt a *little* relieved.
He sniffs the air, then shrugs.
He thinks for a moment, then opens his mouth, but closes it again. Then finally raises his hands:
His grip is strong, sweaty, and warm. He's trying to project and inspire confidence.
Silence. He watches your hand anxiously.
The would-be leader is cutting some futuristic shapes on the floor, sweating profusely.
The would-be leader looks beat. "Okay," he nods.
The would-be leader pulls out a card from his jacket pocket and hands it you. The name reads: 'Pete Andre.'
The young man immediately bounces up and down, then assumes the same dance pattern, embellishing it with some sort of waving motion.
The young man looks startled for a moment, but then flashes you his most winsome smile.
The young speedfreak is silent.
Their would-be leader is less amused.
You see a youngish man bleaching the tips of his hair with a toothbrush. He puts the toothbrush down and extends his hand in greeting.
"*Alright*, man!" He claps his hands, enthusiastically...
"*Really...?*" He sounds relieved.
"...and Egg Head."
"...or because I'm balding, yes. I want to fuse the remains of my hair together, before it leaves me."
"A programmer? That's odd. What was she like? Did you ask her about the nightclub?"
"A shame." He sighs. "What can we do now? Do you see a way out of this jam -- and into a laser-lit future of dance and unity?"
"Above my hair, man!"
"Acele's right. He's one of us now."
"All of Revachol is gonna flock in here."

"Alright!" Andre grins as if this settles it. "It's going to take us a bit to move our stuff inside. A couple of hours, maybe. Come check back later!" He waves to the other speedfreaks. "Let's get moving!"
"Alright!" He grins. "It's going to take us a bit to move our stuff inside. A couple of hours, maybe. Come check back later!" Andre waves to the other speedfreaks. "Let's get moving!"
"Alright!"
"Alright, man!" He claps his hands enthusiastically.
"Alright. Do what you gotta do, man. We trust you." He looks at his posse, then back at you, smiling. "If you need any help, let us know."
"An underground place with no name? Sounds like something the crab-man would say."
"And sadder yet because the dopeheads and burnouts holed up in there are *the worst* kind."
"And the mosaic sidewalk."
"And they have roots in ancient mass society." He pauses. "And they're the custodians of the Perikarnassian Church. Plus they anoint the innocence. They, like, made the innocentic system, no?"
"And yet mysterious." He looks around the church as light beams wash over the dance floor, bathing it in violet blue.
"And you can't just evict her?"
"And... what about the side business? Have you made up your mind?"
"And... you haven't changed your mind about our little side business, have you?"
"And... you're still sure about keeping out our little side business, right?"
"And...?" He tenses up. "What happened?"
"Anyway, now that it's settled... how did she seem? I mean, disposition-wise, about the dance club idea? 'Ja' oder 'Nein'? Rockin' it or droppin' it?"
"Anyway... That's all yours to figure out, cop-man."
"Are we?" He looks at you mysteriously.
"Aw man, really?!" His smile wanes slightly. "You're a complete ballbuster."
"Basically what you need to find here is a tape with some banging music on it, so that Egg Head could use it to remix van Eyck's jam."
"Be careful in there, officer. And tell us how it goes, yeah? We'll be here."
"Besides, did you know that *smell experiences* are all the rage now at the most forward-thinking venues?"
"Born ready," says Andre.
"Brilliant!" He claps his hands. The air in the tent feels lighter. "Noid, the key!"
"But he's likely up to no good." Andre shakes his head. "He's a crab-man, man... a menace to society."
"But you can just evict them, right? You're the law, man. You've got this." He seems to be getting jittery with excitement.
"But you didn't talk to him?" He hums to himself. "I think you should go back -- figure out the situation, see what he wants."
"But you still are..."
"C'mon man, you're killing us..." Andre runs his hands through the spikes of his hair.
"C'mon man..." He looks surprised. "Really?"
"C'mon! Get in and close the flap behind you! The warm stuff is getting out!"
"C'mon! Get in, the warm stuff is getting out."

"C'mon, man, at least *think* about it first. It's our lives at stake here, our *dreams!* I'm sure you'll see things differently once you've let me explain it... You guys like questions, right? Cops *love* questions, ask me some! You'll see!"
"C'mon, man. Who will you trust, a spooky programmer or us? We just wanna make the world a better place."
"Come now, it'll take weeks to get everything set up, start making the produce, and deliver it around to the needy. This is a lengthy process."
"Come on, man! Just talk to her -- I'm sure there's a workaround. Pretty please? We can run the club without bothering her."
"Come on, man. You've gotta talk to her for us!" He attempts to conceal his disappointment.
"Come to think of it, I've never really looked them up, you know. I can't give you a precise definition, but they're a very powerful religious organization."
"Cool, man! Yeah! Look around as much as you wanna, this is *your* place too!"
"Cool, man! Yeah, we should light her up with disco lights. People are gonna lose their shit when they see a club for anodic music with this kind of... sacred shit."
"Could be, we don't know for sure. But we do know they are *spooky*."

"Don't be offensive, Noid. We could use a partner on the other side. It's safer with someone watching over the operation, keeping the... khm..." he clears his throat, "other cops out of our soup. How does 35% sound?"
"Don't be too hard on yourself if you don't figure it out. I think the jam's already pretty ultra."
"Don't let all that 'technology' fool you." He makes little quotation marks with his fingers when he says *technology*. "Where do you think drugs come from?"
"Dunno what happened between you guys, but it was not cool. You should go out and talk to him."
"Easy, Egg. We're still hardcore music venue organisers, first and foremost. But maybe this *does* make us pillars of the local community..."
"Ecstatic vibrations! Totally transcendent! And I've finished setting up the new compressor too!" He looks at the imposing black box in the corner that's churning out the sound.
"Enough now, Noid, you have had enough fun bothering our guest with your crazy theories. Leave him alone."
"Ether? I don't smell ether. Do you, Noid?"
"Everybody letting it *all* hang out -- elite entertainment zone."
"Exactly! It was going fine -- a month ago the place was empty, then suddenly it's all spooked up."
"Exactly! That's *exactly* what we thought!"
"Excellent! Good luck, my friend." He smiles wide, like a replica of his friend with the large head.
"Fine... I guess we're truly done." He sighs.

"Fine..." He seems disappointed. "We can make do. It's going to take us a bit to move our stuff inside. A couple of hours, maybe. Come check back later." Andre waves to the other speedfreaks. "Let's get moving!"
"Fuck yeah, I knew it!"
"Fuck..." Andre frantically smashes buttons. "I can't shut it up, the signal's passed... It's not *in* here! It's..."
"God damn it," you hear Andre say to himself over the thumping beat, "this dance club idea might just work out."
"Good idea."
"Good, good."
"Goodbye, officer."
"Got it! There's no need to get anyone else involved. "He wipes the sweat off his head. "Okay, man, listen..."
"Guys, what's going on?" There's alarm in the man's voice, as he steps back to scan the surroundings. A slight rattle like crystal clattering in the cupboard fills the air, joining the chorus.
"Had a good rest there?"
"He's a quiet man, mostly communicates through music... and by being a master of ceremonies."
"He's coming around." He nods at his friend, then turns to you with a mischievous grin: "You're *getting* it."
"Hello, I'm Andre. It's a pleasure to meet you."
"Hey man, who knows what she's on about." He scoffs. "I get it, she doesn't want us in the church. She's got something against us."
"Hey man, you've stood there for like... half an hour!" The hedgehog-haired man yells from across the coldness of the church.
"Hey now!" He furrows his brow. "I'm 70% sure they're substance abusers."
"Hi again. Have you changed your mind? You changed your mind, right?" The tips of his hair are sharp and white. The bleach has consumed almost all of the toothbrush on the mirror in front of him.
"Hi again. So, uh... How're things going?" He looks excited. The tips of his hair are sharp and white. The bleach has consumed almost all of the toothbrush on the mirror in front of him.
"Hm." He sounds disappointed. "But do let us know if something changes in the church..."
"Hmm... But she's in there somewhere, *has* to be. Have you tried investigating the machines?" He tilts his head, one hand touching the spikes in his hair. "Anyway, do let us know if you see her..."
"Hmm... but you *did* see the machines, right? And the spooky water basins set up in a ritualistic circle in the middle of the church?"
"Hope I remember those moves, man!"
"How about 50%? It's more than a fair deal. We good?"
"Hush, Noid."
"I apologize for my friend Noid's potty-mouth. *I* realize this is not how you speak to a police officer. He has authority issues."
"I asked Noid to install a measure against more drifters wandering in. A padlock. It's a temporary fix. Just something to contain the situation."
"I bet you did! Those were *some* advanced moves, man."
"I can already see it, crème de la crème of Revachol..."
"I didn't want to say it, but it *was* pretty lame of you to imply otherwise. Anyway, you got more questions?"
"I don't know..." He pauses to think. "What does anything mean, really?"
"I don't... even know what to say to that."
"I dunno, man... doesn't it feel like a major hindrance to you?" He rubs his jaw. "A spooky guy climbing around when all the guests are trying to have nice friendly hyper-time?"
"I get it! Okay, man..." He's still shaking a bit...
"I guess it does."
"I guess that's that."
"I have a major sinus infection. Stuffy nose. We all do. Shit's all blasted up. Winter. Can't even breathe."
"I have no idea how you arrived at that conclusion, but it's *wrong!* Look, we even have speakers!" He points at the speaker.
"I hear you, friend. What about it?"
"I hope that settles it... or wait..."
"I hope you get to experience one of our light-smell shows sometime, sir," he says with a smile, nodding his blond, spiked head vigorously. "It'll be a blast."
"I hope you get to experience one of our light-smell shows sometime, sir," he says, nodding his blond, spiked head vigorously. "It'll be a blast."
"I knew from the get go we could count on you." He looks at his friends. "We can make this work -- the dance club will have a future!"
"I knew it! The man is back for those sweet, sweet questions!" The young man smiles at you. "What will it be?"
"I knew it..." The would-be leader drops his spiked head between his knees...
"I knew you'd get it. You're one smart cop."
"I meant to say: Not true."
"I should start making the fires now."
"I tell you, they're in there... You just have to give it another go."
"I think it's super hard core, but you're right, it's not *hyper* hard core."
"I think you did an amazing job here, detective. I would have never thought that van Eyck could be improved on -- but you did it, you made it even better than before."
"I understand, detective. I hope we can continue on an amiable path, right? No more misunderstandings, no more lies." He smiles cautiously. "Before you go, is there anything else you need?"
"I wanna show my hair: I don't give a fuck how old you think I am. I'm twenty!"
"I want you to know that's totally chill with us."
"I was born ready, Egg!"

"I was hoping you would be the judge of that, officer. All I can say is, their spookiness is the kind that keeps us from restoring this church into a community centre. And a place of spiritual refuge."
"I'm 70% sure they're substance users. Don't let the 'technology' fool you." He makes little quotation marks with his fingers when he says *technology*.
"I'm dancing!" He performs yet another strange pattern of moves, but it doesn't look very cool or modern. Honestly, it looks kind of lame...
"I'm sorry, but there is no lab equipment. And no drug ingredients."
"I'm super sure they're alive. I mean, c'mon! I'm at least 90%... maybe 85% sure they're still alive."
"I'm sure you'll figure something out. We can manage it with her if we get inside..."
"I'm talking about the church. And I'm not exaggerating! Even a place of spiritual refuge can become a magnet for all sorts of *dopeheads* and *burnouts* if left unattended..."
"I've seen this thing happen before to people partying this hard..."
"If that's okay with her... We only wanna get in the church and spread the joy and ecstasy of music."
"If you do decide to look into the matter of the church, you know where to find us." He flashes you a confident smile.
"If you want to show your appreciation, we could still use your help. Egg is the one to talk to."
"Intriguing. The way I see it... van Eyck based his remix on some famous original piece. Like, a folk song? Something local. Seems you found an initial part with the main melody."
"It does, doesn't it?"

"It was just impossible -- look at us! How are we going to pull a club out of our ass?! We need starter capital, that's all... We were *totally* going to turn the church into the wickedest club for anodic music in, like, ever..."
"It was this dark shape climbing upside down along the ceiling... like some kind of *crab-man*."
"It's a one-speaker system! It's monodynamic. You wouldn't know the first thing about sound reproduction in anodic music! Other speaker... Pffft!"
"It's all cool... we don't need to escalate things. Let's all calm down."
"It's for starting engines, man."
"It's going to take us a bit to move our stuff inside. A couple of hours, maybe. Come check back later!" He waves to the other speedfreaks. "Let's get moving!"
"It's impossible now."
"It's not Amnesia, guys."
"It's not coming down. People are gonna love it. It'll be, like, our *thing*." His friend keeps dancing. "Plus it keeps the cold and the rain out!"
"It's not!" He looks at your hand near your holster. His eyes fill with fear.
"It's not!" His eyes are wide with fear.
"It's okay, Egg. It's all okay..." He's still shaking from the tension.
"It's the one they sell at the fuel station."
"It's to express my individuality."
"Just like.... before we do we need to earn a bit of dough, do some real work! Get things going, you know."
"Keep us updated about the situation." He thrusts his toothbrush towards you. "Maybe we can help somehow."
"Like I told you, spooky assholes moved in while I was getting all this stuff together. A month ago the place was empty and now it's all spooked up."
"Like... you aren't *alone*, you know?"
"Make up your mind, first it's the sweat, then it's the ether..." He smiles nervously.
"Man... now... now, man... now..." The would-be leader stutters with excitement.
"Maybe... uh... I guess we'll figure something out. Okay, but what about the other spooker -- the one in grandma's clothes? Did you see her?"
"Mellow, man! Mellow!" yells his friend. "No one's a mass murderer, this is a house of *love!*"
"Meteo. A country. On Mundi?" He looks at you, squinting his eyes to see if you're kidding. "On the Mundi isola."
"Mhm?"
"Nah, man, don't worry, he's just dehydrated. Happens all the time in night clubs. He'll recover."
"Nah, man, don't worry, he's mainly dehydrated. It's a regular party reaction, yeah."
"Naw, you just raved too hard. The beat gets so hard, you know, and you were rolling super hard on it..."
"No idea, man."
"No shit..." He sounds tired.

"No worries. We'll figure it out." The man nods enthusiastically, then leans in and whispers: "If co-existing fails, you can always muscle her out, right? If... it's all okay with you. What do you think?"
"No! It's not *true* is what I meant!"
"No, Noid! Stop twisting my melon, man! People are gonna love it. It'll be our *thing*..." His friend disagrees. "Plus it keeps the cold out!"
"No, Noid. He's right... maybe we've approached it the wrong way after all. I'm sure there's a workaround. We can make a deal not to bother her."
"No, Noid. No hammer. I'm sure there's a workaround. We can, like, make a deal not to bother her? You know, co-exist."
"No, it has to be bigger than Hard Core." Andre looks worried as he comes to this realization. "Yes, it has to be even bigger than *Hard Core to the Mega*, it has to be bigger than the scene!"
"No, it's beautiful. Beautiful and brave! Like we want it to be."
"No, man! They're spooky alright. It's just that they would also probably call the police if we started cooking speed in there."
"Noid!" Andre hisses. "No need to escalate things. It's okay, let's all calm down."
"Noid!" Andre turns to his friend. "Let's be reasonable here! We could use a friendly face in the station." He turns back to you with a wide smile on his face.
"Noid's right. You've helped us so much, it's the right thing to do."
"Noid, don't bother our guest with your games."
"Noid, give him the wallet."
"Noid-man! Mellow out," the dancing hedgehog yelps at his friend. "Stop aggroing the law!"
"Not exactly. We've just seen someone who we think is a woman go in and out of the church. A couple of times. And we felt someone... or some *thing*... eyeing us inside. But... that's kinda it."
"Not long. Like a week maybe?" He shrugs.
"Not that we would know *anything* about that. Noid just likes to relay stuff."
"Not twenty."
"Not, like, you know, in a dangerous way," he throws Egg Head an uneasy glance, "or, well, we're not going to do it in a dangerous way."
"Now imagine if we could do that, right? But with, like, a *thousand* people?"
"Now the only thing left to do is the name of the club. Will you do the honours, detective?"
"Of course it is, otherwise I'd just be another poor guy with no education and no money. General-issue, man. Now I'm all that -- *and* I have radical spikes."
"Of course!" He gives you a knowing nod. "I meant the bar, obviously. Why am I even talking about this?" Andre grins as if this settles it.
"Of course. Noid, give the officer the key."
"Officer, I apologize... Noid doesn't always understand the joy of giving for the sake of giving. I think it may have something to do with his childhood."
"Oh geez, please don't do that. There's enough exploitation in the world."
"Oh man! Who is he, what did you think?"
"Oh man, the crab-man, you mean! Who is he, what did you think?"
"Oh my god..." The speedfreaks' would-be leader stands slack-jawed in disbelief at the hard-coreness on display. He whispers to himself: "No way..."
"Oh yeah, sure, this is *exactly* what we need."
"Oh yeah, that's a Meteoran name for the Founding Party. Thought it'd be cool to use it."
"Oh yeah, turn him into a communist, c'mon! It would be super!"
"Oh! Oh! You should have the key. We had to padlock the door to the church to keep more vagrants from wandering in... Noid, give the officer the key!"
"Oh! The old 'Ultra'... we.... uhm..."
"Oh!" Andre almost falls over backward from the realization. "Is *that* why they call you Egg Head, because..."
"Oh, and it felt like there was some *thing* in there with us, watching us from the dark..."
"Oh, hey, man! It's good to see you." He dances over to you in an inexplicably soft-core manner. It's embarrassing.
"Oh, if it was just like that," he rushes to reassure you, "it would be fine. But they're also *spooky*."
"Oh, okay." He nods his bleached, spiked head. "I won't do that anymore."
"Oh, so you met her? Good, good."
"Oh, so you've met her? Good, good." He nods.
"Oh, that's all fine, of course" he rushes to reassure you. "But these people -- they're also *spooky*."
"Oh, the God of Dance is back! I'm dancing with the God of Dance!" He dances over to you, moving in a slightly less lame manner.
"Oh, there you are, man. Don't worry, I've seen this happen before to people partying too hard. You're dehydrated and all. Can you get up?"
"Oh, there you are, man. Don't worry, I've seen this happen before to people partying too hard. You're dehydrated and all."
"Oh. Well, it really is him. It's an honest to god van Eyck beat. Well, actually a reworking of a Pepi Popikarnassos track, but let's not get too deep into that whole mess."
"Oh?" He doesn't know what to say.
"Okay!" He sounds very happy.
"Okay, I'm sorry."
"Okay, man, okay...." You can see his hands shaking a little.
"Okay, man, okay..." He's shaking. "Don't do anything rash! We didn't mean to fuck you over."
"Okay, man, okay." He raises his hands.
"Okay, okay, we're not doing The Return." Andre turns to you and shrugs. "Sorry, cop-man. Got anything else?"
"Okay, we'll try to do it without the drugs." He raises his head from between his knees.
"Okay. That's cool with us, right?" He looks around.
"Okay. We're all cool now, right?" He sounds hopeful. "What's the next step? What's gonna happen now?"
"Okay?" He looks around. There are no objections. "I want you to know there's no bad blood here."
"Really? Huh... interesting. What's he doing in the church?"
"Really?" He smiles, happier than he's ever been before. "We are grateful, cop-man. You're a true ally and the augury of a new era of *ANODIC DANCE MUSIC*."
"Relax. People pass out while partying hard all the time. You're just dehydrated."
"Report back to me when you've done so, alright? We're counting on you!"
"Right? There's something really odd about him... what's he doing in the church anyway?"
"Saint-G is the boulevard before the canal bridge. The one that takes you to the Whirling-in-Rags and the Industrial Harbour. It's got the lanterns and the---"
"Sell some fucking speed, okay? Produce and sell speed."
"Shut the fuck up, Egg!"

"So you're gonna look into it, right?" He turns to you. "It *should* be a police matter -- getting them out. Whatever spooky stuff they're doing, I'm sure it's not what the Ecclesiastes meant their property for."
"So... what now?"
"So...?" He rubs his chilled hands together.
"Some chemicals when mixed can, you know, change colour, or sort of -- blow up..."
"Sorry." He points his thumb at the lieutenant. "We barely have room for one."
"Sure, man. Tell us what you wanna know, let's do it!"
"Sure, why not! Yeah!"
"Sure. What?"
"Thank you, Egg Head..."
"Thank you, we just thought it was the right thing to do."
"That must have been the crab-man. It's okay if you got spooked and ran away." He hums to himself. "I think you should go talk to him -- figure out the situation, see what he wants."
"That's fine, we can manage." He grins, excited.
"That's mega cool, man, you coming in and accusing her of not being human like that. Right on, man!"
"That's mega cool, man, you coming in here and questioning religious symbolism like that. Right on."
"That's mega cool, man, you coming up with theories in here like that. Right on."
"That's mega cool, man, you coming up with wild left-wing stuff in here like that. Right on!"

"That's pretty down-beat. I think I speak for all of us when I say we expected the law to be more open to the idea of love, unity, and the Perikarnassian posse. Especially since you're the one who helped us get inside the church." He looks around.
"That's pretty down-beat. I think I speak for all of us when I say we expected the law to be more open to the idea of love, unity, and the Perikarnassian posse."
"That's the spirit!"
"That's..." He waves his hands. "C'mon, that's..."
"The *spooky* kind."
"The Return? What's that?!"
"The key..." He cautiously hands you the yellow keyring.
"The name..." He appears to mull it over, one hand idly touching his hair. "Everything I manage to come up with sounds just *wrong*."
"The sound above my hair!"
"The what now?" He leans in to hear you better.
"There's a record store in Jamrock, but that's a bit far away... Maybe some local shopkeeper or handyman can help you fix it?"
"They're *spooky*."
"Things are just so, so hard for an entrepreneur in this city right now! It's not like we lied when we said we wanna turn the church into the wickedest club in East Revachol..."
"Things are just way too hard for an entrepreneur in this city. It's not like we're *not* gonna turn the church into the wickedest club in East Revachol..."
"This is gonna bring Revachol together."
"This is my posse: Noid...."
"This is my posse: Noid..." He pauses with his hand still hanging in the air.
"This place is wa-aaaay *under* the underground."
"This? Oh, we're trying to see if we can come up with some cool new special effects to add to the visual aspect of our club experience..." He gestures toward the set-up proudly.
"Together with Acele Berger -- who's out there right now, doing some *seriously* progressive sonic experimentation -- we like to think of ourselves as 'music venue organizers.'"
"Too modern," Andre shakes his spiky head. "And too ironic. We don't want ironic, we want *real*. Real and true and beautiful, like a morning after the rave."
"Totally." There isn't a trace of doubt in his voice.
"Truth is, I don't really know. None of us do. I don't even know how many there are... all we've seen are glimpses."
"Try to squeeze in a promo spot while you're on-air, we've got to start putting the word out."
"UNITY!"
"Uh... c'mon, that was just the crab-man. You're a brave cop, maybe you should go back and talk to him. Figure out the situation, see what he wants."
"Uhm, basically, yes it is."
"Uhm, which other one? I'm not as in tune with my emotions as you are, Egg."
"Uhm... sure." He picks one up from the corner and hands it to you. "Here you go, officer -- the Nosa! Blast away!"
"Uhm..." Andre doesn't know what to say. "It's cold man, you've been looking at that window for like forever now, man. You should dance, get some warmth!"
"Uhm..." He doesn't knows how to comment on what you just said.
"WAIT!!!"
"We appreciate it." He grins. "It's going to take us a bit to move our stuff inside. A couple of hours, maybe. Come check back later!" Andre waves to the other speedfreaks. "Let's get moving!"
"We are grateful, cop-man. You're an augury of a new era of *ANODIC DANCE MUSIC*." The speedfreak smiles, happier than he's ever been before.
"We can continue on an amiable path, right? No more misunderstandings, no more lies." He nods, smiling cautiously. "Before you go, is there anything else you need?"
"We can figure something out, right, guys? Work out a deal. We can run the club without bothering her."
"We don't have any more money! You robbed us blind."
"We have many in the pipeline, officer."
"We just gotta turn it into a speed lab *first*."
"We just... need to turn it into a speed lab before."
"We know she has a problem, man. We're working on it. She didn't exactly have a smooth adolescence."
"We were talking about... the padlock I think?"
"We'll do a straight up club in there, spinning the maddest reels and nothing but, I swear to god! Okay, Egg?"
"We're getting derailed here. In short, you can talk to Noid about the machines. He'll tell you more."
"We've got some serious range on this baby." He nods. "It'll blast her shoes off, believe me."
"Well, I'm sad to say, that's exactly what happened. Sad because we were just about to put Martinaise on the map with one of the maddest dance clubs in Jamrock -- no, strike that -- in Revachol..."
"Well, honestly, I can't. But I am."
"Well, if you ever decide to change your mind, then we're here." He taps the wooden crate he's sitting on. "Just ask me about the door again."
